Assuming you mean India, for ~60 employees across two states, I’d shortlist these three:

Option	Approx. cost for 60 staff*	Best for	Main trade-off
greytHR Essential	~₹2,945/mo	Best overall value	Attendance/advanced HR requires Growth
Zoho Payroll Professional	~₹3,600/mo	Clean, affordable payroll + Zoho ecosystem	Less HR depth than a full HRMS
RazorpayX Payroll	Higher	Payroll + salary disbursement	More expensive at this headcount

*Before GST, using currently published pricing. greytHR charges ₹2,495/month for 50 employees + ₹45 per employee above 50, making 60 employees about ₹2,945/month. 
greythr
+1
 Zoho Professional is ₹3,000/month for 50 + ₹60 per additional employee, or about ₹3,600/month for 60. 
Zoho
+1

1. greytHR — my default pick

Why: At 60 employees, it gives you a very good balance of payroll, statutory compliance, leave and basic HR without paying for a large HR suite. It supports payroll and compliance workflows and has been built specifically around the Indian payroll/HR market. 
greythr

The Essential plan is enough if your main requirement is payroll + leave + employee records. If you also need attendance, shifts, overtime, permissions or geo-fencing, look at Growth, currently ₹4,495/month + ₹85 for employees above 50. 
greythr

Best if: Finance/HR wants a mature Indian payroll system and you expect the company to grow to 100–200+ people.

2. Zoho Payroll — best low-cost alternative

At 60 people, Professional works out to roughly ₹3,600/month before GST. It includes core payroll, statutory deductions, salary payments, payslips, TDS worksheets, F&F and other payroll workflows. 
Zoho
+1

The big advantage is the broader Zoho ecosystem. If you're already using Zoho Books, Zoho Expense or Zoho People, the integration story becomes much more attractive.

Best if: You already use Zoho or want a relatively lightweight payroll product rather than a full HRMS.

3. RazorpayX Payroll — best if salary payments matter

I'd consider RazorpayX if you're already heavily invested in RazorpayX for company banking/payments and want payroll and salary disbursement tied closely together.

The trade-off is price. Zoho and greytHR are currently more compelling on pure payroll-software cost at a 60-person company. Zoho itself notes RazorpayX Payroll's published pricing starts at ₹2,499/month and scales differently by plan/headcount. 
Zoho

Best if: Convenience of payroll → salary payment → banking reconciliation is worth paying extra for.

What I'd check before signing

For 60 employees across two states, don't choose based only on the monthly SaaS price. I'd specifically test:

State-wise Professional Tax — make sure both states are supported correctly.

PF / ESI / TDS — ask who handles updates when statutory rules change.

Multi-state employee transfers — can an employee move from State A to State B without creating messy historical payroll?

Full & Final settlement — gratuity, leave encashment, notice pay and arrears.

Salary revisions + arrears — especially mid-month revisions.

Attendance integration — if you're currently using a biometric/attendance system.

Salary disbursement — direct bank integration vs merely generating a bank file.

Accounting integration — especially if you use Tally, Zoho Books or another accounting system.

Payroll audit trail — who changed salary, bank account, deductions, etc.

Support during month-end payroll — this matters more than fancy HR features.

Data export — make sure you can export employee and payroll history if you switch later.

Pricing at 100/150 employees — don't optimize only for today's 60 employees.

My ranking for your situation

🥇 greytHR — best overall value and safest default
🥈 Zoho Payroll — best if you want simple payroll / already use Zoho
🥉 RazorpayX Payroll — best if integrated salary banking is important

If this is for a 60-person startup/company, I'd personally demo greytHR Essential and Zoho Professional side-by-side first. The difference is small enough that usability and your existing accounting/banking stack should decide it, not the ₹600–700/month price difference.
